issues.text: The main limitation is the lack of linked administrative tax data: tax participation and payments are self-reported, so the outcome measures may be unreliable and the paper's central claims depend on survey declarations.
issues.quote: the authors do not have access to tax administrative data linked to the survey elicitations. As a result, the measures of tax participation and tax payments are self-reported

issues.text: Requiring receipts as proof of tax payment produced many missing values on the tax payment outcome, which are imputed as zeros; this can make the treatment effect estimate on that variable noisy.
issues.quote: this requirement resulted in a considerable mass of missing values on this outcome variable, which are imputed as zeros. This can lead to a noisy measure of the treatment

issues.text: The evaluator asks whether an alternative outcome based on indirect measures of liabilities could be constructed from other survey data, to serve as a robustness check for the tax payment outcome.
issues.quote: I wonder whether some of the information elicited in the survey can be used to construct an indirect measure of liabilities paid by the MIEs, as an alternative outcome variable for robustness checks.

issues.text: It is unclear how tax payments were made (through tax collectors or voluntary compliance), and this dimension of heterogeneity is not explored.
issues.quote: did the enumerators collect information about how the tax payment was made (through tax collectors or via voluntary compliance)?

issues.text: The sample size and sample selection raise external validity concerns; the paper does not sufficiently show how the firms are representative of MIEs in Togo, developing countries, or sub-Saharan Africa.
issues.quote: elaborate a bit more on how the selected firms are representative of the typical MIE context in Togo and, more broadly, across developing countries

issues.text: The paper does not sufficiently explore MIEs' experiences and interactions with tax officials (frequency, perception, audits), which are needed to support the proposed mechanisms; the suggestive evidence in Table 8 is not fully developed.
issues.quote: A dimension not sufficiently explored in the study, in my view, is the role of MIEs' experiences with tax officials.

issues.text: The description of how the treatment was delivered is insufficient; the knowledge transfer process and enumerator homogeneity are unclear, and heterogeneity by enumerator is not examined.
issues.quote: How did the enumerators conduct the knowledge transfer? On page 11, the authors refer to an information packet and consultation, but more details on this process would help

issues.text: The identification relies on a simple comparison of means; the evaluator requests matching or stratification-based weighting (e.g., Coarsened Exact Matching) as a robustness check.
issues.quote: As a robustness check, I suggest complementing this approach with a matching procedure.

issues.text: The proposed mechanism that civic knowledge makes firms assert rights and self-declare more accurately is only plausible rather than established; other explanations, such as a bomb-crater effect of audits, need to be tested and remain undisentangled.
issues.quote: Potential robustness, and future research can help disentangling other potential explanations behind the result.

issues.text: The paper's discussion of the literature on information and tax enforcement is incomplete and should be integrated into the concluding sections.
issues.quote: Some discussion on the literature exploring the role of information in shaping tax enforcement effectiveness could be integrated into the concluding sections

issues.text: The policy and welfare implications (more legitimate or fairer tax system, increased overall revenue) are speculative and not directly supported by the evidence presented.
issues.quote: The authors speculate that this could potentially lead to a more equitable and legitimate tax system by improving firms' understanding
